code_first.q: Apply AND logic to a simplified authentication and file-permission check.
code_first.code:
signedIn = true
allowedToRead = false
if signedIn AND allowedToRead then
    print("Access permitted")
else
    print("Access denied")
endif
p: Change allowedToRead to true and predict again.
Explain the difference between authentication and authorisation. Why does AND require both?
code_first.a: Initially Access denied. With both signedIn and allowedToRead true it prints Access permitted. Authentication establishes who a user is; authorisation checks what that user may access. AND requires both conditions. This is a simple access-rule model, not real authentication.

original_exam_questions: State AND output when A=1, B=0. [1 mark]
Write OR outputs for inputs 00,01,10,11. [4 marks]
Explain NOT output for input 0. [2 marks]

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: For AND, both conditions must be true. Being signed in is not the same as having permission.

stretch.task: Add an OR output to the same simplified access test and compare its result when signedIn=true but allowedToRead=false.
stretch.hint: Test signedIn AND allowedToRead, then signedIn OR allowedToRead. Discuss why the latter is unsafe for access control.
stretch.answer: AND is false and OR is true. Using OR for this rule could allow access when only one of the two required conditions holds.
